window_tier.rule: after the <=4 family is contradicted, a fresh <=4 symbolic learner is initialized with the observation of the contradiction step and fed every later (action, observation); when it is contradicted or exhausts its budget it is restarted from that step's observation (restart count recorded). It is used only when the published v0.1.1 tier would be suffix1 (family contradicted and the <=5 margin not supported or with empty support): if the window is supported with support S, p=(1-eps)*r+eps/4 with r = suffix1 restricted to S and renormalized; forecast_source='window_n4'. Otherwise the v0.1.1 rule is unchanged (v090 / margin_n5 / suffix1). The window never certifies; status, reason and certificate are never changed by it.

experiment_rule.name: one-step certifiability lookahead, uniform over the family support (LU)
experiment_rule.definition: for each action a in {0,1}: score(a)=0 if the <=4 family or the <=5 margin is not 'supported' or a residual-surprise alarm is set. Otherwise S=family.predict_support(a) and score(a)=(1/|S|)*sum_{c in S} N(a,c), where N(a,c) is the number of b in {0,1} such that, after updating COPIES of the family and margin beliefs with (a, full observation c), the family copy is supported, its predict_support(b) is a single code x, the margin copy is supported with predict_support(b)==(x,), and the family copy is not saturated (some row uses < 4 states). A copy that exceeds its row budget or is contradicted counts as not supported. Scores are rounded to 12 d.p.
experiment_rule.choice: argmax score; exact tie -> the default (passive) action, which in study-004 is bgr89.worlds.actions(seed,44)[i]
experiment_rule.certification_unchanged: the policy only chooses the next action; predict/certification code is the frozen v0.1.0 gate order with the v0.1.1 fallback probabilities; no certification rule changes
experiment_rule.geometric_reading: Inferred: the version space is the set of surviving rows; the policy picks the action whose expected next observation most often collapses the region to a single point on the queried coordinate (next code for some action), confirmed by the 5-state margin. Entropy policies bisect volume instead and were Rejected on design data (DISCOVERIES D1).
experiment_rule.design_evidence_Simulated: LU and LP (published-probability weights) gave identical decisions on all 504 study-003 cases (DISCOVERIES D4); LU is chosen because the independent reference recomputes it without the v0.89 catalogue term.

arms.A_active: brute.active.ActiveBruteLearner, actions chosen by experiment_rule (default = passive action)

arms.baselines: uniform ln 4 and SuffixFrequency contexts 1/2/4 (alpha 0.7) on the A and on the P trajectory

metrics.dual_coverage: policy-independent coverage: at each post-burn-in step both predict(0) and predict(1) are evaluated before acting; dual coverage = (number of certified (step, action) pairs)/(2 x steps). Each counterfactual certificate is checked against the evaluator's hidden next emission for that action (drift4: bgr90.worlds.step). predict is side-effect-free; only the taken action's forecast is recorded as issued.
metrics.on_policy_coverage: certified fraction of the taken action, reported (Inferred to overstate learning because the active policy steers into well-known regions, DISCOVERIES D2)
metrics.false_certificate: any conditional or public certificate (taken or counterfactual action) whose code differs from the evaluator truth
metrics.drift_steps: drift4 trace steps 12, 23, 34 (bgr90.worlds.step perturbs t>0, t%11==0)

G1_in_family_soundness.threshold: for arms A and P: 0 false conditional certificates and 0 false public certificates on every in_family case, all 44 steps incl. burn-in, for the taken action AND the counterfactual action (dual)

G2_ood5_soundness.threshold: for arms A and P: 0 false conditional certificates on ood5, all steps, taken and counterfactual action

G3_prime_drift4.threshold: for arms A and P separately (taken action): drift4 false certificates at non-drift steps = 0 AND total drift4 false certificates <= 0.5 x the v0.90 control false certificates on the same cases
G3_prime_drift4.pre_registered_risk: Simulated on design data: the active policy issued 13 drift4 false certificates (passive 4), one at a non-drift step (seed 1290002, mask 0.1, step 13, one step after the drift-12 jump). A may FAIL the non-drift clause; a failure is reported as a failure.
G3_prime_drift4.reported: counterfactual-action drift4 false certificates by step type; post-jump analysis (steps 13, 24, 35)

G4_public_safety.threshold: arms A and P: 0 public certificates on ood5 and drift4; 0 wrong public certificates anywhere

G5_false_alarm_limit.threshold: per arm A and P: fraction of in_family cases with >=1 RESIDUAL_SURPRISE alarm <= 0.05

G6_active_coverage_gain.threshold: (a) pooled in-family dual coverage gain A - P >= 0.05, pooled = unweighted mean over the 5 in_family families of the per-family post-burn-in dual coverage difference; (b) the 95% seed-clustered paired bootstrap CI of the pooled gain (2000 resamples, numpy default_rng seed 20261025, seeds resampled with replacement within each family, per-family statistic = sum of A-P dual-certified pairs over the seed's 3 mask cases / sum of pairs) has lower bound > 0; (c) every in_family family has gain >= -0.01
G6_active_coverage_gain.reported: on-policy coverage, per-mask gains, selective risk

G7_open_world_no_regression.threshold: mean post-burn-in log-loss of the taken action: (a) P <= C on ood5 and on drift4; (b) A <= C on ood5 and on drift4; (c) every arm <= ln 4 on ood5 and drift4 and min published probability >= eps/4 = 0.005 at every step of every family
G7_open_world_no_regression.pre_registered_risk: Simulated on design data without the window tier: A drift4 1.1729 vs C 1.1556 (regression); with the window tier, passive drift4 1.142. (b) on drift4 may FAIL.
G7_open_world_no_regression.reported_targets: drift4 P below suffix1 (paired bootstrap, seed 20261025, CI excluding 0); per-mask table

G8_passive_equivalence.threshold: (a) at every step of every case P and C have identical status, reason, certificate and public certificate, and identical probabilities at every step where P's forecast_source != 'window_n4'; (b) A in-family mean post-burn-in log-loss per family <= C + 0.05 nats

G9_retraction_semantics.threshold: BRUTE_PLAN_003 G8 wording (amendment A4) for arms A and P; plus: no (step, certificate) pair appears twice in any issued or retraction list, and ActiveBruteLearner.record_issued called twice for the same forecast records it once (tests/test_brute_active.py)

G10_compute_budget.threshold: peak rows <= 160000 for the family, margin and window learners of A and P; every family/margin budget exhaustion yields ABSTAIN/BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; lookahead copies that exceed the budget score 0 (counted: lookahead_budget_hits)
G10_compute_budget.reported: peak lookahead copy rows, wall-clock per arm (target A <= 4 x C; design: about 2-3x)

G11_independent_audit.threshold: experiments/v020_independent_reference.py (no import of brute; bgr89/bgr90 world and baseline modules allowed; supports from experiments/v90_independent_reference.py) recomputes for arms A and P every <=4 and <=5 support (taken and counterfactual action), decision, saturation, surprise, residual, alarm, post-contradiction probability and forecast_source including the window tier, every retraction reason, every experiment score and every chosen action; P-vs-C equality (G8a) rechecked; 0 mismatches

bridge_items.B1_issuance: bridge report: calling predict twice at the same step through brute.api/1.1 double-records issuance (service_v011._predict calls record_issued on every CERTIFIED predict). Fixed in v0.2.0 by de-duplicating (step, certificate) in ActiveBruteLearner.record_issued; brute.api/1.1 is frozen and keeps the bug (documented). Study counts: Exact by code reading, run_case_003 calls predict and record_issued once per step; verified on the sealed study-003 traces in BRUTE_DEVIATIONS_004.md.
bridge_items.B2_tests: bridge report: a fresh clone of main fails 3 tests. Cause (Exact): .gitattributes '*.ps1 text eol=crlf' makes checkout write BGR-All-One.ps1 with CRLF while MANIFEST.sha256 records the committed LF bytes (deviation D5 of study-003), so test_manifest_matches_tracked_files and test_fast_verify_passes fail; test_verify_fails_under_tampered_results is the known A3 version error. Fix: '*.ps1 -text' so checkout is byte-identical to the committed blob (= the BGR original), and correct the README test count.
bridge_items.B3_api_1_2: brute.api/1.2 (brute/api/service_v020.py): new op 'experiment' and response field experiment={action, score, scores, rule, tie_break, per_action:{family_code_rows, family_open_rows, family_rows, margin_rows}}; forecast_source may be 'window_n4'.
